details: Effective August 23, 2026, the European Union has prohibited transactions with HTX (formerly Huobi Global SA) and ten other crypto and payment platforms as part of tightened sanctions against Russia. This measure aims to prevent sanctions circumvention, directly barring EU persons and entities from direct or indirect dealings. Users holding balances on these platforms must withdraw funds or seek explicit authorization from national central banks. This move legally enforces prior platform actions blocking EU users and could trigger tax events for those forced to sell assets.
title: EU Bans Transactions with HTX, 10+ Crypto Platforms Over Russia Sanctions

details: The cryptocurrency market has seen a significant rally, driven by several key US developments. The US Treasury's expanded debt buyback plan has injected liquidity, while President Trump's push for the CLARITY Act and a proposed SEC crypto-regulation framework have fostered optimism for regulatory clarity. This combination led Bitcoin to surge approximately 23% in August, and Ethereum jumped around 29%, reaching $2,472 by August 24, 2026. The rally was also marked by substantial short liquidations and strong institutional inflows into both Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs.
title: US Treasury Buybacks, Regulatory Clarity Drive Crypto Surge

details: Crude oil prices saw a decline on August 24, 2026, in anticipation of a new round of aggressive US sanctions against Iran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a major financial campaign targeting Iran's economy, warning that nations continuing business with Tehran could face isolation. These escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly concerning the Strait of Hormuz, are expected to maintain oil price volatility through the second half of 2026, contributing to global risk aversion in financial markets.
title: US Sanctions on Iran Set to Boost Oil Volatility, Global Risk

details: The United States is reportedly preparing to implement a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods, a move that would increase President Trump's second-term duties on China to approximately 20%. This potential tariff is part of a Section 301 investigation into excess manufacturing capacity and precedes a scheduled meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September. Separately, Canada faces a proposed 50% tariff on certain goods. These rising trade tensions could impact global supply chains, economic stability, and overall market sentiment.
title: US May Impose New 7.5% Tariffs on Chinese Goods
